verses.original: Καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς πάλιν εἶπεν ἐν παραβολαῖς αὐτοῖς λέγων
verses.transliteration: Kai apokritheis ho Iēsous palin eipen en parabolais autois legōn
verses.literal: Once again Jesus spoke . . . to them in parables
verses.literalPt: ENTÃO Jesus, tomando a palavra, tornou a falar-lhes em parábolas, dizendo:

verses.original: Ὡμοιώθη ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ βασιλεῖ ὅστις ἐποίησεν γάμους τῷ υἱῷ αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: Hōmoiōthē hē basileia tōn ouranōn anthrōpō basilei hostis epoiēsen gamous tō huiō autou
verses.literal: The kingdom of heaven is like a king who prepared a wedding banquet for his son
verses.literalPt: O reino dos céus é semelhante a um certo rei que celebrou as bodas de seu filho;

verses.original: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν τοὺς δούλους αὐτοῦ καλέσαι τοὺς κεκλημένους εἰς τοὺς γάμους καὶ οὐκ ἤθελον ἐλθεῖν
verses.transliteration: kai apesteilen tous doulous autou kalesai tous keklēmenous eis tous gamous kai ouk ēthelon elthein
verses.literal: He sent his servants to call those he had invited to the banquet but they refused . . . to come
verses.literalPt: E enviou os seus servos a chamar os convidados para as bodas, e estes não quiseram vir.

verses.original: Πάλιν ἀπέστειλεν ἄλλους δούλους λέγων Εἴπατε τοῖς κεκλημένοις Ἰδοὺ τὸ ἄριστόν μου ἡτοίμακα οἱ ταῦροί μου καὶ τὰ σιτιστὰ τεθυμένα καὶ πάντα ἕτοιμα δεῦτε εἰς τοὺς γάμους
verses.transliteration: Palin apesteilen allous doulous legōn Eipate tois keklēmenois Idou to ariston mou hētoimaka hoi tauroi mou kai ta sitista tethymena kai panta hetoima deute eis tous gamous
verses.literal: Again he sent other servants and said Tell those who have been invited that I have prepared my dinner My oxen and fattened cattle have been killed and everything is ready Come to the wedding banquet
verses.literalPt: Depois, enviou outros servos, dizendo: Dizei aos convidados: Eis que tenho o meu jantar preparado, os meus bois e cevados já mortos, e tudo já pronto; vinde às bodas.

verses.original: Οἱ δὲ ἀμελήσαντες ἀπῆλθον ὃς μὲν εἰς τὸν ἴδιον ἀγρόν ὃς δὲ ἐπὶ τὴν ἐμπορίαν αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: Hoi de amelēsantes apēlthon hos men eis ton idion agron hos de epi tēn emporian autou
verses.literal: But they paid no attention and went away one to his field another to his business
verses.literalPt: Eles, porém, não fazendo caso, foram, um para o seu campo, outro para o seu tráfico;

verses.original: οἱ δὲ λοιποὶ κρατήσαντες τοὺς δούλους αὐτοῦ ὕβρισαν καὶ ἀπέκτειναν
verses.transliteration: hoi de loipoi kratēsantes tous doulous autou hybrisan kai apekteinan
verses.literal: The rest seized his servants mistreated them and killed them
verses.literalPt: E os outros, apoderando-se dos servos, os ultrajaram e mataram.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ βασιλεὺς ὠργίσθη καὶ πέμψας τὰ στρατεύματα αὐτοῦ ἀπώλεσεν τοὺς φονεῖς ἐκείνους καὶ τὴν πόλιν αὐτῶν ἐνέπρησεν
verses.transliteration: Ho de basileus ōrgisthē kai pempsas ta strateumata autou apōlesen tous phoneis ekeinous kai tēn polin autōn eneprēsen
verses.literal: The king was enraged and he sent his troops to destroy those murderers and burn their city
verses.literalPt: E o rei, tendo notícia disto, encolerizou-se e, enviando os seus exércitos, destruiu aqueles homicidas, e incendiou a sua cidade.

verses.original: τότε λέγει τοῖς δούλοις αὐτοῦ Ὁ μὲν γάμος ἕτοιμός ἐστιν οἱ δὲ κεκλημένοι οὐκ ἦσαν ἄξιοι
verses.transliteration: tote legei tois doulois autou Ho men gamos hetoimos estin hoi de keklēmenoi ouk ēsan axioi
verses.literal: Then he said to his servants The wedding banquet is ready but those I invited were not worthy
verses.literalPt: Então diz aos servos: As bodas, na verdade, estão preparadas, mas os convidados não eram dignos.

verses.original: πορεύεσθε οὖν ἐπὶ τὰς διεξόδους τῶν ὁδῶν καὶ ὅσους ἐὰν εὕρητε καλέσατε εἰς τοὺς γάμους
verses.transliteration: poreuesthe oun epi tas diexodous tōn hodōn kai hosous ean heurēte kalesate eis tous gamous
verses.literal: Go therefore to the crossroads . . . . . . and invite to the banquet as many as . . . you can find
verses.literalPt: Ide, pois, às saídas dos caminhos, e convidai para as bodas a todos os que encontrardes.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐξελθόντες οἱ δοῦλοι ἐκεῖνοι εἰς τὰς ὁδοὺς συνήγαγον πάντας οὓς εὗρον πονηρούς τε καὶ ἀγαθούς καὶ ἐπλήσθη ὁ γάμος ἀνακειμένων
verses.transliteration: Kai exelthontes hoi douloi ekeinoi eis tas hodous synēgagon pantas hous heuron ponērous te kai agathous kai eplēsthē ho gamos anakeimenōn
verses.literal: So the servants went out into the streets and gathered everyone . . . they could find both evil and good and the wedding hall was filled with guests
verses.literalPt: E os servos, saindo pelos caminhos, ajuntaram todos quantos encontraram, tanto maus como bons; e a festa nupcial foi cheia de convidados.

verses.original: Εἰσελθὼν δὲ ὁ βασιλεὺς θεάσασθαι τοὺς ἀνακειμένους εἶδεν ἐκεῖ ἄνθρωπον οὐκ ἐνδεδυμένον ἔνδυμα γάμου
verses.transliteration: Eiselthōn de ho basileus theasasthai tous anakeimenous eiden ekei anthrōpon ouk endedymenon endyma gamou
verses.literal: But when the king came in to see the guests he spotted a man who was not dressed in wedding clothes
verses.literalPt: E o rei, entrando para ver os convidados, viu ali um homem que não estava trajado com veste de núpcias.

verses.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ Ἑταῖρε πῶς εἰσῆλθες ὧδε μὴ ἔχων ἔνδυμα γάμου Ὁ δὲ ἐφιμώθη
verses.transliteration: kai legei autō Hetaire pōs eisēlthes hōde mē echōn endyma gamou Ho de ephimōthē
verses.literal: Friend he asked how did you get in here without wedding clothes But the man was speechless
verses.literalPt: E disse-lhe: Amigo, como entraste aqui, não tendo veste nupcial? E ele emudeceu.

verses.original: Τότε ὁ βασιλεὺς εἶπεν τοῖς διακόνοις Δήσαντες αὐτοῦ πόδας καὶ χεῖρας ἐκβάλετε αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ σκότος τὸ ἐξώτερον ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων
verses.transliteration: Tote ho basileus eipen tois diakonois Dēsantes autou podas kai cheiras ekbalete auton eis to skotos to exōteron ekei estai ho klauthmos kai ho brygmos tōn odontōn
verses.literal: Then the king told the servants Tie him hand and foot and throw him . . . into the outer darkness where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth
verses.literalPt: Disse, então, o rei aos servos: Amarrai-o de pés e mãos, levai-o, e lançai-o nas trevas exteriores; ali haverá pranto e ranger de dentes.

verses.original: Πολλοὶ γάρ εἰσιν κλητοὶ ὀλίγοι δὲ ἐκλεκτοί
verses.transliteration: Polloi gar eisin klētoi oligoi de eklektoi
verses.literal: For many are called but few are chosen
verses.literalPt: Porque muitos são chamados, mas poucos escolhidos.

verses.original: Τότε πορευθέντες οἱ Φαρισαῖοι συμβούλιον ἔλαβον ὅπως αὐτὸν παγιδεύσωσιν ἐν λόγῳ
verses.transliteration: Tote poreuthentes hoi Pharisaioi symboulion elabon hopōs auton pagideusōsin en logō
verses.literal: Then the Pharisees went out and conspired . . . . . . to trap Jesus in His words
verses.literalPt: Então, retirando-se os fariseus, consultaram entre si como o surpreenderiam nalguma palavra;

verses.original: καὶ ἀποστέλλουσιν αὐτῷ τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτῶν μετὰ τῶν Ἡρῳδιανῶν λέγοντες Διδάσκαλε οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἀληθὴς εἶ καὶ τὴν ὁδὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐν ἀληθείᾳ διδάσκεις καὶ οὐ μέλει σοι περὶ οὐδενός οὐ γὰρ βλέπεις εἰς πρόσωπον ἀνθρώπων
verses.transliteration: kai apostellousin autō tous mathētas autōn meta tōn Hērōdianōn legontes Didaskale oidamen hoti alēthēs ei kai tēn hodon tou Theou en alētheia didaskeis kai ou melei soi peri oudenos ou gar blepeis eis prosōpon anthrōpōn
verses.literal: They sent their disciples to Him along with the Herodians Teacher they said we know that You are honest and that You teach the way of God in accordance with the truth You seek favor from no one because You pay no attention to external appearance . . .
verses.literalPt: E enviaram-lhe os seus discípulos, com os herodianos, dizendo: Mestre, bem sabemos que és verdadeiro, e ensinas o caminho de Deus segundo a verdade, e de ninguém se te dá, porque não olhas a aparência dos homens.

verses.original: εἰπὸν οὖν ἡμῖν τί σοι δοκεῖ ἔξεστιν δοῦναι κῆνσον Καίσαρι ἢ οὔ
verses.transliteration: eipon oun hēmin ti soi dokei exestin dounai kēnson Kaisari ē ou
verses.literal: So tell us what You think Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar or not
verses.literalPt: Dize-nos, pois, que te parece? É lícito pagar o tributo a César, ou não?

verses.original: Γνοὺς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὴν πονηρίαν αὐτῶν εἶπεν Τί με πειράζετε ὑποκριταί
verses.transliteration: Gnous de ho Iēsous tēn ponērian autōn eipen Ti me peirazete hypokritai
verses.literal: But Jesus knew their evil intent and said You hypocrites why are you testing Me
verses.literalPt: Jesus, porém, conhecendo a sua malícia, disse: Por que me experimentais, hipócritas?

verses.original: ἐπιδείξατέ μοι τὸ νόμισμα τοῦ κήνσου Οἱ δὲ προσήνεγκαν αὐτῷ δηνάριον
verses.transliteration: epideixate moi to nomisma tou kēnsou Hoi de prosēnenkan autō dēnarion
verses.literal: Show Me the coin used for the tax And they brought Him a denarius
verses.literalPt: Mostrai-me a moeda do tributo. E eles lhe apresentaram um dinheiro.

verses.original: Καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Τίνος ἡ εἰκὼν αὕτη καὶ ἡ ἐπιγραφή
verses.transliteration: Kai legei autois Tinos hē eikōn hautē kai hē epigraphē
verses.literal: Whose image is this He asked . . . and whose inscription
verses.literalPt: E ele diz-lhes: De quem é esta efígie e esta inscrição?

verses.original: Λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Καίσαρος Τότε λέγει αὐτοῖς Ἀπόδοτε οὖν τὰ Καίσαρος Καίσαρι καὶ τὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ τῷ Θεῷ
verses.transliteration: Legousin autō Kaisaros Tote legei autois Apodote oun ta Kaisaros Kaisari kai ta tou Theou tō Theō
verses.literal: Caesar’s they answered . . . So Jesus told them Give to Caesar what is Caesar’s and to God what is God’s
verses.literalPt: Dizem-lhe eles: De César. Então ele lhes disse: Dai pois a César o que é de César, e a Deus o que é de Deus.

verses.original: Καὶ ἀκούσαντες ἐθαύμασαν καὶ ἀφέντες αὐτὸν ἀπῆλθαν
verses.transliteration: Kai akousantes ethaumasan kai aphentes auton apēlthan
verses.literal: And when they heard this they were amazed So they left Him and went away
verses.literalPt: E eles, ouvindo isto, maravilharam-se, e, deixando-o, se retiraram.

verses.original: Ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ προσῆλθον αὐτῷ Σαδδουκαῖοι λέγοντες μὴ εἶναι ἀνάστασιν καὶ ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν
verses.transliteration: En ekeinē tē hēmera prosēlthon autō Saddoukaioi legontes mē einai anastasin kai epērōtēsan auton
verses.literal: That same day the Sadducees who say there is no resurrection came to Jesus and questioned Him
verses.literalPt: No mesmo dia chegaram junto dele os saduceus, que dizem não haver ressurreição, e o interrogaram,

verses.original: λέγοντες Διδάσκαλε Μωϋσῆς εἶπεν Ἐάν τις ἀποθάνῃ μὴ ἔχων τέκνα ἐπιγαμβρεύσει ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀναστήσει σπέρμα τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: legontes Didaskale Mōusēs eipen Ean tis apothanē mē echōn tekna epigambreusei ho adelphos autou tēn gynaika autou kai anastēsei sperma tō adelphō autou
verses.literal: Teacher they said Moses declared that if a man dies without having children his brother is to marry the widow and raise up offspring for him
verses.literalPt: Dizendo: Mestre, Moisés disse: Se morrer alguém, não tendo filhos, casará o seu irmão com a mulher dele, e suscitará descendência a seu irmão.

verses.original: ἦσαν δὲ παρ’ ἡμῖν ἑπτὰ ἀδελφοί καὶ ὁ πρῶτος γήμας ἐτελεύτησεν καὶ μὴ ἔχων σπέρμα ἀφῆκεν τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: ēsan de par’ hēmin hepta adelphoi kai ho prōtos gēmas eteleutēsen kai mē echōn sperma aphēken tēn gynaika autou tō adelphō autou
verses.literal: Now there were seven brothers among us The first one married and died without having children So he left his wife to his brother
verses.literalPt: Ora, houve entre nós sete irmãos; e o primeiro, tendo casado, morreu e, não tendo descendência, deixou sua mulher a seu irmão.

verses.original: ὁμοίως καὶ ὁ δεύτερος καὶ ὁ τρίτος ἕως τῶν ἑπτά
verses.transliteration: homoiōs kai ho deuteros kai ho tritos heōs tōn hepta
verses.literal: The same thing happened to . . . the second and third brothers down to the seventh
verses.literalPt: Da mesma sorte o segundo, e o terceiro, até ao sétimo;

verses.original: ὕστερον δὲ πάντων ἀπέθανεν ἡ γυνή
verses.transliteration: hysteron de pantōn apethanen hē gynē
verses.literal: And last of all the woman died
verses.literalPt: Por fim, depois de todos, morreu também a mulher.

verses.original: ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει οὖν τίνος τῶν ἑπτὰ ἔσται γυνή πάντες γὰρ ἔσχον αὐτήν
verses.transliteration: en tē anastasei oun tinos tōn hepta estai gynē pantes gar eschon autēn
verses.literal: In the resurrection then whose wife will she be of the seven For all of them were married to her
verses.literalPt: Portanto, na ressurreição, de qual dos sete será a mulher, visto que todos a possuíram?

verses.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Πλανᾶσθε μὴ εἰδότες τὰς γραφὰς μηδὲ τὴν δύναμιν τοῦ Θεοῦ
verses.transliteration: Apokritheis de ho Iēsous eipen autois Planasthe mē eidotes tas graphas mēde tēn dynamin tou Theou
verses.literal: Jesus answered - You are mistaken because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God
verses.literalPt: Jesus, porém, respondendo, disse-lhes: Errais, não conhecendo as Escrituras, nem o poder de Deus.

verses.original: ἐν γὰρ τῇ ἀναστάσει οὔτε γαμοῦσιν οὔτε γαμίζονται ἀλλ’ ὡς ἄγγελοι ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ εἰσιν
verses.transliteration: en gar tē anastasei oute gamousin oute gamizontai all’ hōs angeloi en tō ouranō eisin
verses.literal: In the resurrection people will neither marry nor be given in marriage Instead they will be like the angels in heaven
verses.literalPt: Porque na ressurreição nem casam nem são dados em casamento; mas serão como os anjos de Deus no céu.

verses.original: περὶ δὲ τῆς ἀναστάσεως τῶν νεκρῶν οὐκ ἀνέγνωτε τὸ ῥηθὲν ὑμῖν ὑπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ λέγοντος
verses.transliteration: peri de tēs anastaseōs tōn nekrōn ouk anegnōte to rhēthen hymin hypo tou Theou legontos
verses.literal: But concerning the resurrection of the dead have you not read what - God said to you
verses.literalPt: E, acerca da ressurreição dos mortos, não tendes lido o que Deus vos declarou, dizendo:

verses.original: Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ Θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ καὶ ὁ Θεὸς Ἰσαὰκ καὶ ὁ Θεὸς Ἰακώβ οὐκ ἔστιν ὁ Θεὸς νεκρῶν ἀλλὰ ζώντων
verses.transliteration: Egō eimi ho Theos Abraam kai ho Theos Isaak kai ho Theos Iakōb ouk estin ho Theos nekrōn alla zōntōn
verses.literal: I am the God of Abraham the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob He is not the God of the dead but of the living
verses.literalPt: Eu sou o Deus de Abraão, o Deus de Isaque, e o Deus de Jacó? Ora, Deus não é Deus dos mortos, mas dos vivos.

verses.original: Καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ ὄχλοι ἐξεπλήσσοντο ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: Kai akousantes hoi ochloi exeplēssonto epi tē didachē autou
verses.literal: When the crowds heard this they were astonished at His teaching
verses.literalPt: E, as turbas, ouvindo isto, ficaram maravilhadas da sua doutrina.

verses.original: Οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι ἀκούσαντες ὅτι ἐφίμωσεν τοὺς Σαδδουκαίους συνήχθησαν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό
verses.transliteration: Hoi de Pharisaioi akousantes hoti ephimōsen tous Saddoukaious synēchthēsan epi to auto
verses.literal: And when the Pharisees heard that Jesus had silenced the Sadducees they themselves gathered . . . . . . together
verses.literalPt: E os fariseus, ouvindo que ele fizera emudecer os saduceus, reuniram-se no mesmo lugar.

verses.original: καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν εἷς ἐξ αὐτῶν νομικὸς πειράζων αὐτόν
verses.transliteration: kai epērōtēsen heis ex autōn nomikos peirazōn auton
verses.literal: One of them an expert in the law tested Him with a question
verses.literalPt: E um deles, doutor da lei, interrogou-o para o experimentar, dizendo:

verses.original: Διδάσκαλε ποία ἐντολὴ μεγάλη ἐν τῷ νόμῳ
verses.transliteration: Didaskale poia entolē megalē en tō nomō
verses.literal: Teacher which commandment is the greatest in the Law
verses.literalPt: Mestre, qual é o grande mandamento na lei?

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ ἔφη αὐτῷ Ἀγαπήσεις κύριον τὸν Θεόν σου ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ καρδίᾳ σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ ψυχῇ σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ διανοίᾳ σου
verses.transliteration: Ho de ephē autō Agapēseis kyrion ton Theon sou en holē tē kardia sou kai en holē tē psychē sou kai en holē tē dianoia sou
verses.literal: Jesus declared Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind
verses.literalPt: E Jesus disse-lhe: Amarás o Senhor teu Deus de todo o teu coração, e de toda a tua alma, e de todo o teu pensamento.

verses.original: αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ μεγάλη καὶ πρώτη ἐντολή
verses.transliteration: hautē estin hē megalē kai prōtē entolē
verses.literal: This is the first and greatest commandment
verses.literalPt: Este é o primeiro e grande mandamento.

verses.original: δευτέρα δὲ ὁμοία αὐτῇ Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν
verses.transliteration: deutera de homoia autē Agapēseis ton plēsion sou hōs seauton
verses.literal: And the second is like it Love your neighbor as yourself
verses.literalPt: E o segundo, semelhante a este, é: Amarás o teu próximo como a ti mesmo.

verses.original: ἐν ταύταις ταῖς δυσὶν ἐντολαῖς ὅλος ὁ νόμος κρέμαται καὶ οἱ προφῆται
verses.transliteration: en tautais tais dysin entolais holos ho nomos krematai kai hoi prophētai
verses.literal: All the Law and the Prophets hang on these two commandments
verses.literalPt: Destes dois mandamentos dependem toda a lei e os profetas.

verses.original: Συνηγμένων δὲ τῶν Φαρισαίων ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτοὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς
verses.transliteration: Synēgmenōn de tōn Pharisaiōn epērōtēsen autous ho Iēsous
verses.literal: While the Pharisees were assembled Jesus questioned them
verses.literalPt: E, estando reunidos os fariseus, interrogou-os Jesus,

verses.original: λέγων Τί ὑμῖν δοκεῖ περὶ τοῦ Χριστοῦ τίνος υἱός ἐστιν Λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Τοῦ Δαυίδ
verses.transliteration: legōn Ti hymin dokei peri tou Christou tinos huios estin Legousin autō Tou Dauid
verses.literal: What do you think about the Christ Whose son is He David’s they answered
verses.literalPt: Dizendo: Que pensais vós do Cristo? De quem é filho? Eles disseram-lhe: De Davi.

verses.original: Λέγει αὐτοῖς Πῶς οὖν Δαυὶδ ἐν Πνεύματι καλεῖ αὐτὸν Κύριον λέγων
verses.transliteration: Legei autois Pōs oun Dauid en Pneumati kalei auton Kyrion legōn
verses.literal: Jesus said to them How then does David in the Spirit call Him Lord For he says
verses.literalPt: Disse-lhes ele: Como é então que Davi, em espírito, lhe chama Senhor, dizendo:

verses.original: Εἶπεν Κύριος τῷ Κυρίῳ μου Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου Ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου Ὑποκάτω τῶν ποδῶν σου
verses.transliteration: Eipen Kyrios tō Kyriō mou Kathou ek dexiōn mou Heōs an thō tous echthrous sou Hypokatō tōn podōn sou
verses.literal: The Lord said to my Lord Sit at My right hand until . . . I put Your enemies under Your feet
verses.literalPt: Disse o Senhor ao meu Senhor: Assenta-te à minha direita, Até que eu ponha os teus inimigos por escabelo de teus pés?

verses.original: Εἰ οὖν Δαυὶδ καλεῖ αὐτὸν Κύριον πῶς υἱὸς αὐτοῦ ἐστιν
verses.transliteration: Ei oun Dauid kalei auton Kyrion pōs huios autou estin
verses.literal: So if David calls Him Lord how can He be David’s son
verses.literalPt: Se Davi, pois, lhe chama Senhor, como é seu filho?

verses.original: Καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐδύνατο ἀποκριθῆναι αὐτῷ λόγον οὐδὲ ἐτόλμησέν τις ἀπ’ ἐκείνης τῆς ἡμέρας ἐπερωτῆσαι αὐτὸν οὐκέτι
verses.transliteration: Kai oudeis edynato apokrithēnai autō logon oude etolmēsen tis ap’ ekeinēs tēs hēmeras eperōtēsai auton ouketi
verses.literal: No one was able to answer a word and from that day on no one dared to question Him any further
verses.literalPt: E ninguém podia responder-lhe uma palavra; nem desde aquele dia ousou mais alguém interrogá-lo.
